column8: At 35 weeks, unwell on a Friday after her OB office closed, unsure where to go.
column9: if I get worse i.e. fever, vomiting, etc am I supposed to go to L&D triage/my normal ob? or urgent care? My OB office closed at noon today so I can’t call them to ask.

column8: UK couple from abroad, one school-age child, birth date set; nobody family-side can come.
column9: We're both from abroad and there's no way we can get any family members here to help us during this precious time.

column8: Finding someone to keep her child overnight and do the school run.
column9: Somebody will need to stay with our child and even though there were a few friends who said they could do it, there's only one who offered a sleepover for our child. As it's Tuesday evening, someone will need to take our child to school the following day or to look after them until my partner is ready to collect them. I don't want to be a burden to anyone..

column8: The paid option she rules out.
column9: I know we could get a babysitter to stay over but I can't imagine paying £150+ for that.

column8: Considering going to hospital alone so her partner can do the school run.
column9: Now, the other option is for me to go to the hospital by myself and then for my partner to join me in the morning once he's dropped our child off at school. Has anyone done that?

column8: What she has heard about second labours.
column9: as it's the second labour, apparently it is quicker and easier? Is this really the case?

column8: Why she would rather labour alone than have an exhausted partner afterwards.
column9: The last thing I'd want would be for him not to have any sleep and then once I've given birth I'd have to go collect my child from school and look after the newborn bc he's tired and had no sleep at all. If that makes any sense. At the end of the day I'd rather be there on my own and have a fresh and full of energy partner who can look after two children (well, a child and a baby) and offer support to me.

column8: Selling her own car for a family car in her fiancé's name; feels her independence going.
column9: I feel like pregnancy and being a FTM takes away so much independence with finances anyway and this feels hard even though I know I should be so grateful?

column8: How costs are split.
column9: I’ll be paying for us both to be insured on it and the tax but he pays 90% of the bills and now has bought us a car

column8: Booked for a planned birth at 39 weeks; her mother's reaction.
column9: My mum said today that she's annoyed I wont feel the agony of a natural birth (in the context of a kind of revenge or "now you get it" type way) which just hurt because I spent a lot of time trying to mentally prepare myself for that pain

column8: How people brush off her worries.
column9: It's just brushed off as, its fine, at least you wont feel the pain, at least you know when itll happen etc etc.

column8: What family told her before her birth plan changed.
column9: before I knew I was going to need one, I just got the classic scary stories from family saying its the worst, and all the graphic details.

column8: Feeling alone with it.
column9: Im the last one in my family to have a baby but the first of my friends. Its just leading me to become quite detached from people and feel pretty isolated.

column8: Nobody can tell her where to get information before her birth date.
column9: Ive tried asking a few members of hospital staff and GPs where I should go for info and they just tell me to call the maternity hotline at the hospital. I had been under the impression that was for emergencies, not general info

column8: Replying to a commenter about the weeks after the birth.
column9: Like you said, people tend to focus more on the baby than the mum and its definately something I was ignorantly unaware of before becoming pregnant.

column8: How fast her birth plan changed late in pregnancy.
column9: I went in for some very rushed ecvs ( withing 2 days of each other) and then before I knew it, ive been booked in for the c section. I still haven't had a sit down consultation or anything.

column8: First pregnancy at 28 weeks; a surgical PA frustrated that midwife visits explain nothing.
column9: All they do when I go in is say “do you have questions” and then do a Doppler. There has  not been a single visit where they went over what is normal and what to expect unless they were answering a specific question that I asked.

column8: The midwife's answer when she asked whether birth would be discussed.
column9: I asked if we would be talking about birth at any of these visits and she basically said no, they don’t want to “overwhelm me with information.”

column8: Her question about the hospital class, and the midwife's answer.
column9: Do I need to pay $250 and spent 2 hours every week for 6 weeks in a birthing class to just get a little information about what to expect?  When I asked the midwife that she just said “you can use YouTube.” D:

column8: After following the YouTube advice.
column9: I did that and then was accused of using “Dr Google” by the same person who told me to use YouTube for birth education.

column8: Deciding to pay for the hospital class after all.
column9: It’s $250 for the classes at the hospital and they don’t do tours ever since Covid :/ at this point I’m just gonna pay for the classes though after she told me they’re not going to talk about what to expect during birth at these visits.

column8: What the hospital offers instead of a tour, and the class cost.
column9: all they have is a video on the website that tells you where to check in and what the room looks like. And the classes offered are what I mentioned in the post - $240 and they don’t take our employee insurance for them and I freaking work at this hospital

column8: Seven months pregnant with her first, paid to look after a friend's baby full time.
column9: I’m currently getting paid to watch her child through the government.

column8: What she fears when she returns to minding her friend's child.
column9: I’m scared I won’t be able to fully give myself to my own first born child in the way I originally wanted to because I will have to care for my friend’s child.

column8: Why she can't stop.
column9: This job is also easing the financial burden and allows my husband and I to live a more comfortable lifestyle. Plus my friend really depends on the child care (like I said, she can’t really afford it otherwise).

column8: At 23 weeks, HR refused the change her doctor's note asked for.
column9: My HR told me today that due to working with aggressive clients being a core function, I cannot receive this accommodation.

column8: The options HR offered instead.
column9: The only thing they could do is get a different note that specifies only working with my base clients who have not shown aggression and then they can't guarantee 30 hours a week.  Or I can go on short term disability and get paid $400 less.

column8: Plus-size, 34 weeks with her second, frustrated at how care treats her.
column9: I’m SO sick of my weight ALWAYS being a reason for them to treat me different.

column8: Why her readings are not taken by hand at the hospital.
column9: I tell them to do my BPs manually and they literally (MFM & triage - whom are both location IN THE HOSPITAL) told me they do not have the size cuff they need for my arm. Are you kidding me ?!

column8: What she would do for a third pregnancy.
column9: I think if I have a third down the road I’ll be going across the river to the next state for care cause I can’t deal with this a third time

column8: Two days past her due date, on leave from a kitchen job.
column9: Im on maternity leave because i work as a kitchen manager and couldnt handle the work load anymore.

column8: Guilt about her husband covering the bills.
column9: I feel guilty for being on leave because my husband is carrying the load of all our bills now with help from his family which i greatly appreciate but dont want to accept too much of.

column8: Waiting while friends have their babies.
column9: Im just sad and lonely, all my friends are having or have had their babies and im just waiting on mine.

column8: Before her 40+5 appointment.
column9: i dont want the doctor to think im over dramatic or rude, she is a very nice doctor, i just need to be taken seriously because by the time im at my appointment i will be 40+5, and they promised they wouldnt make me go past 41 weeks.

column8: First-time mother of a one-month-old seeing a different clinician each visit.
column9: We have been to her pediatrician 4 times, and have seen a new person each time which has been VERY frustrating.

column8: Second pregnancy; her partner wants his parents from abroad to stay six months again.
column9: Now with our second child, he has asked them to stay for another 6 months.

column8: How the last long stay went.
column9: The last time they were here, he spent almost every evening hanging out with them and the baby while I spent time alone in my room. It was horribly isolating but his argument was that he never gets to see them anyway, so he would like to spend evenings with them. (They live in a different country)

column8: The compromise her partner offered.
column9: 2m away was the middle ground he was prepared to meet me with. He wanted them to stay for a full 6 months.

column8: First-time mother at 7 weeks with many symptoms, not yet told family.
column9: I feel like people refer to this time of pregnancy as “barely pregnant” but I feel like I’m getting my ass kicked.

column8: Before telling family.
column9: Maybe when family knows I won’t feel so alone in all this, but for now I’m frustrated. Grateful, but frustrated.
